review_scope.structural_evidence: Four draft articles; exact public revisions; required tags; two displayed primary links each; whitespace word counts 186, 187, 193, and 196.
review_scope.method: Blind-solved all four candidates from directly opened AFI Catalog pages before reading research, draft, local key, or legacy material. Then opened every displayed article link and checked each body claim, role binding, answer ambiguity, source relevance, and final frozen raw hash.

checked_claims: The exact displayed Academy event page identifies Tim Robbins as Andy Dufresne and Morgan Freeman as Red, credits Frank Darabont as writer/director, confirms the King novella and its 1982 Different Seasons publication, and identifies Deakins, Francis-Bruce, and Newman as Oscar-nominated collaborators.
The official 67th Academy Awards ledger lists Morgan Freeman, not Robbins, as the film’s Leading Actor nominee and shows the film’s seven nominations without a win.
items.distractor_review: Morgan Freeman played Red, Bob Gunton played Warden Samuel Norton, and William Sadler played Heywood. Tim Robbins alone played Andy Dufresne; all alternates are relevant cast members with distinct roles.

checked_claims: The final displayed AFI page credits Gene Hackman as Jimmy Popeye Doyle, Roy Scheider as Buddy Russo, Fernando Rey as Alain Charnier, and Tony Lo Bianco as Sal Boca; the article’s final Russian text matches AFI’s Sal Boca rather than expanding the name.

AFI supports Friedkin’s induced-documentary technique, improvised dialogue, actors’ research, Egan/Grosso technical consulting, and the Robin Moore book basis while distinguishing the screen narrative from the 1961 case.
The official 44th Academy Awards ledger supports the five wins, Hackman’s Actor win, and Scheider’s Supporting Actor nomination.
items.distractor_review: Fernando Rey played Alain Charnier, Roy Scheider played Buddy Russo, and Tony Lo Bianco played Sal Boca. Gene Hackman alone played Jimmy Popeye Doyle; the alternatives are relevant cast members with distinct roles.

checked_claims: The exact displayed AFI page credits Jon Voight as Joe Buck, Dustin Hoffman as Ratso Rizzo, Sylvia Miles as Cass, and Brenda Vaccaro as Shirley; it also supports Schlesinger, Salt, and the Herlihy-novel adaptation.
The official 42nd Academy Awards ledger confirms the film’s Best Picture, Directing, and adapted-screenplay wins; both Voight and Hoffman were Actor nominees and John Wayne won for True Grit.
items.distractor_review: Dustin Hoffman played Ratso Rizzo, Sylvia Miles played Cass, and Brenda Vaccaro played Shirley. Jon Voight alone played Joe Buck; all alternatives are relevant cast members with distinct roles.

checked_claims: The exact displayed AFI page credits Tom Cruise as Ron Kovic, Willem Dafoe as Charlie, and Kyra Sedgwick as Donna, and supports the Kovic autobiography and Stone/Kovic screenplay collaboration.
AFI distinguishes the early 1976 project, for which Pacino was planned to play Kovic, from the released 1989 film in which Cruise was cast and credited; the draft makes this distinction explicit.
The official 62nd Academy Awards ledger lists Cruise as a Leading Actor nominee and the film’s Directing and Film Editing wins, plus Stone and Kovic’s adapted-screenplay nomination.
items.distractor_review: Willem Dafoe played Charlie and Kyra Sedgwick played Donna. Al Pacino was attached to an earlier unmade 1976 project, not the released 1989 film. Tom Cruise alone played Ron Kovic in the stated film.
